name: Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges
description: A review paper critically examining the current state of Visual Question Answering (VQA) in terms of problem formulation, existing datasets, evaluation metrics, and algorithms. The paper reviews major VQA datasets including DAQUAR, COCO-QA, The VQA Dataset, FM-IQA, Visual7W, and Visual Genome, discussing their limitations and biases, and exhaustively reviews existing algorithms for VQA.
creator: Kushal Kafle and Christopher Kanan, Chester F. Carlson Center for Imaging Science, Rochester Institute of Technology
citeAs: Kafle, K. and Kanan, C. (2017). Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges. arXiv:1610.01465v4 [cs.CV].
rai:dataCollection: Multiple VQA datasets were collected using different methods. DAQUAR used images from NYU-DepthV2 Dataset with manual and automatic annotation. COCO-QA used an NLP algorithm to derive QA pairs from COCO image captions. The VQA Dataset employed Amazon Mechanical Turk workers to generate questions and answers for COCO images and synthetic cartoon images. FM-IQA collected human-generated questions and answers originally in Chinese with English translations. Visual Genome used free-form and region-specific question prompting with crowdsourced annotators. Visual7W is a subset of Visual Genome with additional pointing questions.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Experiments, User-generated content data
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The English version of the FM-IQA dataset was not retrievable from the provided download link at the time of the review.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from: NYU-DepthV2 Dataset (DAQUAR), Microsoft COCO dataset with 328,000 images (COCO-QA, COCO-VQA, FM-IQA, Visual7W), YFCC100M/Flickr100M (Visual Genome, Visual7W), and synthetic cartoon images (SYNTH-VQA). QA pairs were generated by human annotators via Amazon Mechanical Turk or automatically via NLP algorithms.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Datasets released beginning in 2014 through the time of the article (2017).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For COCO-VQA multiple-choice format, 18 answer choices were constructed per question comprising: the correct answer (most frequent annotator answer), three plausible answers collected without seeing the image, the top ten most popular answers in the dataset, and randomly selected correct answers for other questions. For Visual7W pointing questions, four plausible bounding boxes were provided as multiple-choice options.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For COCO-QA, longer sentences from COCO captions were broken into smaller chunks for NLP processing to generate QA pairs, though this caused grammatical errors in many cases. For DAQUAR, a reduced version (DAQUAR-37) was created using only 37 object categories. Visual Genome used both free-form and region-specific question prompting to reduce bias in question types.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For COCO-VQA, Amazon Mechanical Turk workers were asked to 'Stump a smart robot' to generate questions, and a separate pool of workers generated answers. Each question received 10 independent answers. For DAQUAR-consensus, an average of five human-annotated ground truth answers per question were collected. For Visual Genome, annotators used free-form and region-specific prompting to generate QA pairs. For Visual7W, plausible wrong answers were collected by prompting annotators to answer without seeing the image. FM-IQA used human judges to assess answer quality on a 3-point scale (0=totally wrong, 1=partially correct, 2=perfectly correct).
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) was used for COCO-VQA annotation.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-human agreement on COCO-VQA is approximately 83.3% using AccuracyVQA. Over 59% of 'Why' questions have fewer than three annotators giving the same answer. More than 13% of yes/no questions have both 'yes' and 'no' repeated by more than three annotators. Simple questions can evoke diverse answers, including antonyms (e.g., left and right). The consensus-based metric (min(n/3, 1)) awards full score when an algorithm agrees with three or more of ten annotators.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper notes that as of the article's writing, Visual Genome is the largest VQA dataset and no methods beyond author-established baselines had been evaluated on it. No explicit versioning or deprecation policies are described in the paper.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: SYNTH-VQA synthetic human models span different age, gender, and races to provide variation in appearance. The VQA Dataset contains subjective, opinion-seeking questions that may reflect personal perspectives of annotators.
rai:dataSocialImpact: VQA has potential applications as an aid to blind and visually impaired individuals, enabling them to get information about images on the web and in the real world. It could also improve human-computer interaction as a natural way to query visual content, and be used for image retrieval without metadata or tags.
rai:dataBiases: Language bias is a major issue: question-only models achieve up to 50% accuracy on COCO-QA without using images. Yes/no answers span about 38% of COCO-VQA questions, with 59% answered 'yes.' Answering 'yes' to all yes/no questions yields 71% accuracy instead of the expected ~50%. VQA systems are sensitive to question phrasing. MCB-ensemble achieved only 47% accuracy (below chance) on balanced yes/no questions about people, compared to 83% on biased COCO-VQA yes/no questions. COCO-VQA contains many subjective and opinion-seeking questions. Attentive mechanisms may attend to biased regions rather than task-relevant regions.
rai:dataLimitations: DAQUAR is too small for training complex models and contains only indoor scenes with clutter and extreme lighting. COCO-QA has grammatical errors and nonsensical questions due to NLP generation flaws, and only four question types. COCO-VQA has strong language biases enabling image-blind algorithms to achieve 49.6% accuracy. FM-IQA requires human judges for evaluation, making iterative development impractical. Visual Genome's long-tailed answer distribution makes open-ended evaluation challenging. Current datasets are not sufficient to evaluate whether an algorithm has truly 'solved' VQA. Datasets need to be larger, less biased, and use more nuanced per-question-type evaluation.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation of VQA algorithms. Benchmarking visual question answering systems. Evaluating image understanding capabilities. Research into vision-language integration. Potential deployment for assisting visually impaired users and image retrieval systems.
rai:annotationsPerItem: COCO-VQA: 3 questions per image, 10 answers per question. SYNTH-VQA: 3 questions per scene, 10 ground truth answers per question. DAQUAR-consensus: average of 5 human-annotated ground truth answers per question. Visual Genome: average of 17 QA pairs per image.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: NLP algorithm used to automatically generate QA pairs from COCO image captions for COCO-QA. ResNet used to classify bounding boxes during test time in FDA model. Word2vec used to compute similarity between question words and object labels.
